articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Detection and Classification Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Lung cancer is a huge and serious hazard to human health, as it is one of the deadliest cancers for both men and women, owing to its ability to metastasize to other organs. Cancer detection and therapy options remain difficult for experts in this sector. To solve these difficulties, artificial intelligence approaches such as machine learning and deep learning have produced very promising and practical results. Deep learning, in particular, provides extraordinary precision and speed, allowing for the identification of even the smallest pulmonary nodules with extensive information. Several organizations have helped by offering databases to aid scientific study. Among these, the LIDC-IDRI dataset is one of the world's largest publicly available databases. CT images for 1012 patients are included. In this paper, we compared SVM, KNN, DT, and Random Forest machine learning models, as well as VGG19, EffetientNet-V2-L, Wide-Resnet-50-2-weight, and EffetientNet-B7 models.

articleTitle: A New Design of a Multi-Link Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new design of a multilink quadrotor capable of traversing narrow spaces and transporting objects by changing its shape to adapt the geometry while flying. Unlike traditional quadrotors, which need an arm manipulator for transportation, this design makes it possible to reduce its weight. The proposed aerial multilink quadrotor can fly and modify its orientation and position in space without affecting the difference between lift forces provided by its propellers. Instead, the attitude movements can be achieved by adjusting the angles of its links, which allows the optimization of the consumed energy. Furthermore, it can adapt its morphology in flight according to the assigned task to find the most suitable configuration. We have proposed several configurations, each of which can be used to perform the task efficiently and optimally, and identify singular configurations that should be avoided that could render our system uncontrollable.

articleTitle: A Graph ATtention Networks Model for Session-Based Recommender Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In recent years, session-based recommender systems (SBRSs) have emerged as a new paradigm of recommender systems to help users in their different decision-making processes. The goal of SBRSs is to capture dynamic and short-term user preferences within sessions to provide more timely and accurate next-item recommendations that are sensitive to be adapted in different contexts. In the literature, the proposed approaches for SBRS development are limited to some models that lack more precision and efficacy, which are the primary purposes for this kind of recommender system. This paper aims to formally present a graph neural networks model for session-based recommender systems based on Graph ATtention networks (GAT). GAT can capture complex transitions between items through a session modelled as graph-structured data. The effectiveness of the pro-posed GAT-based model is extensively evaluated on three public real-world datasets. Experimental results show the superiority of our model against some used baselines in the SBRS field.

articleTitle: Nonlinear PD Control of Mobile Manipulator Base During Arm Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This work proposes an approach applying Nonlinear Proportional Derivative (NPD) control, commonly used for parallel robots, to a mobile manipulator. The NPD control compensates for coupling effects between the base and the manipulator arm by updating proportional and derivative gains using position and velocity error measurements. Simulation results using AKASHA mobile manipulator models demonstrate the superiority of the nonlinear PD control approach over conventional PID control.

articleTitle: Edge and Texture Analysis for Face Spoofing Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: With the increasing use of biometric technology in various applications of daily life, face spoofing detection technology plays a crucial role in securing them against fraudulent access. In this paper, a new face anti-spoofing method is proposed that involves a two-stage feature extraction from the YCbCr and HSV face images. The first stage extracts the Binarised Statistical Image Features (BSIF) from the Canny edge face images, while the second stage extracts the Local Binary Patterns (LBP) features from the input face images. The resulting feature vectors from both stages are concatenated to match their identification before being fed into a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. Experiments on the publicly available MSU Mobile Face Spoof Database (MSU-MFSD) confirm that the proposed method achieves promising results compared to state-of-the-art face anti-spoofing techniques.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Real-Time Video Watermarking Prototype Using PL-PS Embedded Processor Over Network Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper implements on FPGA a point-to-point video transmission prototype between an FPGA board and a PC as first step using Petalinux based system over an embedded processor in a hardware/software codesign approach, generalized later to the transmission between two ZedBoard FPGA plat-forms using TCP/IP ethernet protocol. The prototype hardware implementation is exploited to implement spatial watermarking for both visible and invisible techniques using additive and Least Significant Bit (LSB) methods respectively. The Prototype performances are evaluated in terms of video transmission, watermarking and hardware implementation complexity.

articleTitle: Constrained Complex System of Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper describes a sophisticated controller suited to high-performance applications. A non-minimum-phase system under constraints is one of the complex systems that requires a precise regulating of parameters to get a process satisfying the required conditions. This mission is difficult for most controllers, especially conventional ones. Predictive Functional Control, part of Model Predictive Control (MPC), is the proposed algorithm to overcome this problem. It is capable of predicting the future behavior of systems and making control decisions accordingly, to stable control and handle complex and non-linear systems, handle constraints on system variables, and provide better disturbance rejection. The benefits and performance of the proposed approach are numerically assessed on the thermal treatment of a metal part with a constraint on the manipulated variable.

articleTitle: Listen First Broadcast Later for Interest Forwarding in Named Data Networks Over LLNs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This study is among the first to explore the adoption of Listen First Broadcast Later (LFBL) for interest forwarding in Named Data Networks (NDN) over Lower Power and Lossy Networks (LLNs). To this end, the performance of LFBL is compared to the existing Probabilistic Flooding (PF) and Deferred Blind Flooding (DBF). Our study demonstrates that LFBL provides superior performance tradeoffs by achieving comparable satisfaction ratios and response times while significantly reducing energy consumption. This advantage stems from LFBL's ability to avoid excessive interest forwarding away from the producer, distinguishing it from DBF and PF. Our findings highlight LFBL as a promising approach for interest forwarding in NDN over LLNs.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent System Based on Dynamic Load Balancing for Collaborative Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Intrusion detection systems contribute to the improvement of the security of systems as well as the confidentiality and integrity of data. These systems are based on traffic analysis, which makes their performance and response time sensitive to the density of network traffic and distributed denial of service attacks. In this paper, we suggest a new collaborative intrusion detection system based on a multi-agent system. The intrusion detection technique relies on dynamic load balancing of traffic analysis to enhance the performance of intrusion detection, especially distributed denial of service attacks. In particular, mobile agents collaborate to analyze traffic using decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks. The results of the experiment, using NSL-KDD public dataset, show that the proposed intrusion detection system architecture improved the performance and the scalability of intrusion detection compared with state of the art techniques.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approaches for Resilient and Sustainable Urban Mobility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The transportation sector is responsible for 23% of energy-related CO2 emissions. Decarbonizing transportation is challenging, as it is still 92% dependent on non-renewable resources. However, current transport decarbonization-related policies are insufficient to decrease CO2 emissions to the expected level. Therefore, strategic approaches to reducing emissions from urban transport are critical to addressing the challenges of climate change. In this talk, we present our recent research activities on a framework to build the next level of innovative data-driven traffic light strategies as the most impactful action to reduce CO2 emissions within the context of urban mobility for Connected and Autonomous Cars. This Framework is committed to embracing the next generation of Edge-AI, benefiting from the ease of implementation and increased computation power toward more composable, distributed, and federated intelligence, as well as security by design frameworks. Powerful eye-bird-view multimodal data fusion approaches feed AI models for accurate CO2 and urban noise level predictions, that feed to dashboards for awareness purposes. Advanced reinforcement learning techniques make use of urban noise predictions to implement the best traffic light strategy in real time. We will also discuss the challenges to achieve resilience by proactively detecting misbehaving entities within Vehicle-to-Everything settings

articleTitle: Optimizing Bilateral Teleoperation Control Architectures: A Comparative Study Under Constant and Variable Time Delays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In this paper, we optimize the set of controllers and parameters in two bilateral teleoperation control schemes: the classic four-channel architecture and the improved wave-transform based delayed bilateral teleoperation architecture, by tuning them using Simulink's Response Optimization tool using the Matlab Optimization toolbox. In both architectures, the master and slave devices are identical 1-dof robots represented by their impedance model. We propose a comparative analysis between the performance of each of the architectures in terms of transparency and stability, in presence of constant and variable time delays. By conducting this comparative study, we hope to contribute to the development of more efficient, robust and user-friendly teleoperation systems, ultimately advancing the state of the art in this field.

articleTitle: UAV-Based Search and Rescue System Using a Probability Distribution Map
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for enhancing search and rescue (SAR) missions using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The framework includes a probability-based mapping technique that identifies areas with the highest probability of target presence using a Probability Distribution Map (PDM). Additionally, optimized waypoint generation techniques are employed to enhance mission efficiency. Furthermore, the framework addresses UA V S’ kinematic and dynamic constraints by incorporating smoothing techniques, namely Dubin and Pythagorean Hodograph curves (PH) for safe and feasible flight trajectories. Extensive simulations show the effectiveness of the proposed SAR framework.

articleTitle: Attitude Stabilization of a Flexible Satellite with Sloshing Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper presents a robust control approach aimed at achieving attitude stabilization of a flexible satellite while effectively mitigating propellant slosh torques. The proposed approach combines a disturbance observer (DO) with a proportional-derivative (PD) controller. Initially, the DO is employed to estimate the lumped disturbances present in the system. Subsequently, a PD controller is designed to stabilize the satellite and attenuate residual disturbances. Through simulation experiments conducted on a flexible satellite model, the efficacy of the proposed approach in achieving asymptotic stability is empirically validated. Thus, the proposed approach is demonstrated to be effective for the stated purpose.

articleTitle: Stochastic Approach to realistic rendering in computer graphics for Virtual Reality (VR)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In Virtual Reality, it is important to make the rendering of images displayed on an HMD headset as realistic as possible. In this case, it is a question of taking into account the multiple reflections, refractions and diffusions using stochastic methods (Monte Carlo, Gaussian processes, etc.) or AI (CNN neural networks). These methods can be used in other fields such as vision, crowd simulation, etc. This Keynote Lecture begins by introducing the different processing necessary for obtaining a computer-generated image such as: geometric modeling, camera parameters, color, photometric quantities, etc. Then it presents in detail the various stochastic rendering methods allowing the generation of synthetic images with a high level of realism. Among these methods we can cite: the Monte Carlo method, Bayesian Monte Carlo, Metropolis, spectral Analysis of Quadrature Rules and Fourier Truncation-based Methods Applied to the Shading Integral, etc. This lecture will be illustrated with realistic images generated with different rendering methods.

articleTitle: Virtual & Augmented Reality for Medical Training and Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Virtual and augmented reality technologies offer opportunities to create training and rehabilitation tools in virtual or augmented environments, giving users a first-person experience. Designing such systems requires defining the most critical components to be simulated, and to what degree they can be successfully simulated, considering the context of their use and the effectiveness of interactions. There are several research questions to which we have provided answers, including: How can the user be represented in the virtual environment, and what is the added value of this representation for medical training purposes? How can interaction fidelity impact user performance in surgical simulation-based training? What is the impact of augmented reality feedback on the performance of a patient's gait rehabilitation process? In addition, I will present two rehabilitation assistance systems for improving patient usability and motivation: 1) for upper limb motor rehabilitation after stroke in virtual reality; 2) gait rehabilitation in augmented reality.

articleTitle: Enhancing Physical Rehabilitation Monitoring through Multi-View Fusion of Human Body Skeleton
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The Kinect has gained popularity in physical therapy and rehabilitation systems as a skeleton body tracking device. However, limitations such as occlusion and noise in skeleton tracking have reduced its reliability. To address these issues, some studies have proposed multi-kinect systems to expand the field of vision and enhance data precision. In this paper, we introduce the design of a 360° multi-view fused human body skeleton system using Kinect devices. Our system harnesses the strengths of the Kinect's Software Development Kit (SDK) and the spatial arrangement of the Kinect devices to estimate the 3D position coordinates of human skeleton joints. Importantly, the system allows for easy customization to accommodate modifications. Our system enables the extraction of indicators related to human walking patterns within the context of physical rehabilitation. These indicators serve to motivate patients, provide valuable feedback, and track their rehabilitation progress. The system demonstrated its utility in initial laboratory tests for physical therapy and rehabilitation monitoring. Our research presents a novel approach to address the limitations of the Kinect in physical therapy and rehabilitation. The preliminary findings from laboratory tests indicate the system's potential to enhance physical therapy and rehabilitation monitoring.

articleTitle: Blockchain, IoT and AI: The Bets are Open!
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Blockchain, IoT and AI are key technologies that revolutionized the world, each one on its side; let's see if the mix of the three can go hand in hand! Blockchain is the ingeniously simple, revolutionary protocol that increases trust, security, transparency, and the traceability of shared data. IoT is at the heart of essential areas like industrial automation, e-Health and smart cities. For its part, AI improves outcomes by detecting patterns and optimizing processes. The convergence between blockchains and AI has been discussed in many works, and the observation is the same for the convergence between blockchains and IoT. However, the question of the convergence of the three technologies altogether remains open. In this talk, I will try to answer questions like: Can these three innovations coexist and complement? Can they remedy each other's weaknesses? What place can they occupy in the context of the next wave of digital transformation?

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Bio-Inspired Clustering in Flying Ad-Hoc Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The Flying Ad hoc NETworks (FANETs) have evolved from the interaction of multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV s) in ad hoc fashion to provide a versatility of applications and services in civilian and military domains. As it ensures cooperation and collaboration between these UAVs, Communication is one of the most crucial issues in the design of FANETs systems. However, the limited resources, in terms of energy, bandwidth utilization, and the mobility patterns of the flying UAVs should be considered when ensuring the information's reliability. This research aims to investigate the routing issue in FANET systems while considering the constraining features presented by these latter. Here, we proposed a new clustering and mobility management strategy for robust data routing in FANETs relying on combining k-means and black-hole algorithms. The simulation of the proposed protocol conducted using Network Simulator 3 (NS3) has yielded convincing results in terms of energy consumption and data communication, outperforming those exhibited by the referred protocols.

articleTitle: Dynamic Transmission Power Adjustment for Enhanced Energy Efficiency and Extended Lifespan of Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic transmission power adjustment technique to enhance energy efficiency and extend the operational lifespan of mobile devices in fog computing environments. By monitoring the locations of surrounding access points and their own locations, mobile devices adapt their transmission power prior to task offloading. The technique employs four transmission power levels: 3.6mW (default) for access points beyond 265m, 2.7mW for distances between 210m and 265m, 1.8mW for distances between 150m and 210m, and 0.9m W for distances less than or equal to 150m. Two key metrics are evaluated: the consumed energy of mobile devices (in Joules) and the remaining operational devices over time. Additionally, the number of offloaded tasks for each transmission power level is analyzed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of dynamic transmission power adjustment in improving energy efficiency, prolonging device lifespan, and optimizing task offloading in fog computing environments. These findings contribute to the advancement of energy-efficient mobile computing and provide valuable insights for future optimizations.

articleTitle: A Single-Channel EEG-Based Discrimination of Major Depressive Disorder with Wavelets Features and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Electroencephalography is largely used as a technique for neuroscience studies and applications. However, using all of its electrode set is not required for every EEG-related problem, especially when reducing the number of channels will lead to an optimized experience by minimizing both time and computational resources. In this study, we tested the possibility of using single-channel EEG signals for prescreening major depressive disorder within a group of 34 depressive patients and 30 age-matched healthy controls. Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) with 4 levels of decomposition was applied on 364 EEG segments in order to extract relevant brain rhythms (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, Gamma). A 364 by 35 matrix of wavelet features was generated and then ranked using the ReliefF algorithm. Features from Delta, theta, and Alpha bands proved to be the most relevant and an accuracy of 97.28 % had been reached by the Decision Tree classifier in conjunction with 10-fold Cross Validation (10-fold CV).

articleTitle: A Virtual Reality-Based Serious Game Designed for Personalized Hand Motor Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Arm and/or hand weakness after a stroke can significantly impair an individual's ability to perform daily tasks and lead a normal life. The primary goal of stroke rehabilitation is to reduce long-term disability, and success requires a personalized approach based on individual patient needs. Throughout this process, health care professionals must provide ongoing support to patients. Researchers are looking into new, low-cost tools to supplement traditional methods and improve patients' quality of life. Virtual rehabilitation is one such tool, which combines virtual reality (VR) technology with functional rehabilitation and serves as a motivational tool for both patients and therapists. Rehabilitation exercises can be tailored to each patient's specific needs and abilities by utilizing VR technology. This paper describes a personalized VR-based system, which includes a serious game for hand rehabilitation, with the goal of providing an engaging and effective tool for stroke patients with hand disabilities.

articleTitle: Development of a Multilingual Vocalization Methodology for Algerian SMS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: We have developed an innovative methodology for the multilingual vocalization of Algerian SMS messages, drawing insights from an initial study that highlights the challenges posed by the complex and specific language used in these messages. In the course of our research, we worked with a dataset comprising 20,000 SMS messages, which, after segmentation, yielded 27,903 French words (class fr) and 42,300 Algerian words (class DZ). This dataset served as the foundation for our comprehensive workflow, outlining the various steps involved in implementing a vocalization system tailored to Algerian SMS messages. Our approach begins with data preprocessing, where we focus on text normalization and the extraction of textual features from these messages. Subsequently, the second phase of our methodology centers on developing a language identification system, recognizing that Algerian SMS messages often encompass multiple languages, including French and Arabic. To tackle this challenge, we employed a range of classifiers, including SVM, KNN, MNB, RFC, RNN, and CNN. Notably, SVM achieved the highest accuracy of 62.56% without SMS normalization. However, it's worth highlighting that the accuracy significantly improved to 73.18% after applying text normalization when using the CNN method. Following the language identification step, we proceed to perform speech synthesis based on the textual content, followed by unit concatenation to generate vocalized SMS messages. The results obtained through our methodology have provided valuable insights into both the strengths and limitations of our developed system, setting the stage for promising avenues of future research in the field of multilingual vocalization of SMS messages in dialects.

articleTitle: Thermal Sensation with Microheater for Virtual Reality Applications: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In this work, we followed an energy-saving approach to design a micro-heater device for virtual reality (VR) applications, using a simple, low-cost step-lithography technique. First, spiral shapes of the Al-0.5Cu-based micro-heaters are designed and fabricated with a surface area of 5 mm x 5 mm. We, then, tested and evaluated the Joule heating characteristics of the proposed micro-heater using the proposed spiral design patterns. The fabricated micro-heaters are, then, used to realize a hand-worn VR device with thermal feedback. We present, in this paper, preliminary results of a wearable device with one micro-heater mounted on the user's index fingertip. The performance of the proposed system is verified under a VR application including touching three glasses with different water temperatures. The results denote that the geometry of the micro-heater enabled the sensation of temperature to be reached with low energy consumption. The proposed micro-structure provides researchers with the possibility to design more compact and lightweight devices for thermal sensation generation in VR applications.

articleTitle: 6G-SECUREIDS: Blockchain-Enhanced Secure Knowledge Transfer for Distributed Intrusion Detection Systems in Advanced Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: As the development of wireless networks advances towards the deployment of 6G technology, ensuring robust security measures becomes crucial. In this paper, we propose 6G-SECUREIDS, a novel intrusion detection system designed specifically for 6G wireless networks. The system leverages machine learning techniques and blockchain technology to detect and mitigate security threats, safeguard data privacy, and ensure efficient and optimized training. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the system, with the clients achieving high accuracy scores across different model architectures. The promising results highlight the potential of 6G-SECUREIDS as a valuable security solution for future 6G networks, contributing to the overall protection and integrity of the wireless communication ecosystem.

articleTitle: SegFormer: Semantic Segmentation Based Tranformers For Corrosion Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Corrosion detection plays a critical role in various industries for ensuring the safety and durability of structures. Traditional manual inspection methods are time-consuming and prone to human error, necessitating the development of automated techniques. In recent years, artificial intelligence and deep learning have shown promise in corrosion detection. This paper focuses on the evaluation of SegFormer, a pretrained model that combines Transformers with semantic segmentation, for corrosion detection. This paper investigates the application of fine-tuned SegFormer, a transformer-based model, for corrosion detection. Initially, challenges are identified due to class imbalance and limited annotations on the semantic dataset. To address this, a specialized corrosion segmentation dataset is created. The fine-tuned SegFormer model achieves promising results on this dataset, accurately detecting corrosion regions with a test loss of 0.2621, mean accuracy of 0.8139, and mean IoU of 0.7116. This study demonstrates the model's potential for corrosion detection and its significance in advancing semantic segmentation for critical applications.

articleTitle: Optimal Path Selection and Producer Allocation for Energy Distribution in Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The Energy Internet (EI) revolutionizes the traditional energy system by establishing a decentralized and inter-connected network. This paradigm shift empowers individuals and communities to actively participate in energy generation, consumption, and trading. Efficient energy routing is a critical aspect of optimizing cost-effectiveness and minimizing power loss in this dynamic landscape. In this paper, we present a novel approach that leverages the Firefly Algorithm for producer selection and the A* algorithm for optimal path-finding. Through extensive experimentation, we demonstrate the efficacy of our proposed method in achieving optimal energy utilization and cost-effectiveness within the evolving Energy Internet.

articleTitle: Optimal PID Control of a Novel Multirotor with Inclined Rotors and Spatial Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This work introduces an innovative multirotor UAV featuring a spatial configuration and inclined rotors to address under-actuation challenges. The modeling of the multirotor is based on the Newton-Euler formalism, accounting for structural asymmetry and non-coincident center of gravity with the body frame origin. In addition, a Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) is used to control the considered drone, and optimal control gains are selected via a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) meta-heuristic algorithm. The simulation results for attitude change with hovering and helical trajectory tracking without changing orientations demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed design and controller. The paper concludes by discussing potential enhancements in mechanical design and control strategies.

articleTitle: Theory and Practice for Trajectory Tracking of Quadrotor UAV Via a Fifth Generation Sliding Mode Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper presents an effective approach for a quadrotor during trajectory tracking seeking fixed-time stabilization and disturbance rejection. The quadrotor is modeled by Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE) while considering lumped disturbances. Theoretical control design and practical implementation are addressed in the paper. Motivated by the variable structure systems in the form of Sliding Mode Control (SMC) theory and homogeneous systems theory, a homogeneous-SMC-based flight control is proposed to achieve robust trajectory tracking along fixed-time stability. First, a Homogeneous Nonlinear Chattering-Free Terminal Sliding Manifold (HNCFTSM) is synthesized. Second, a Fifth Generation-based Fixed-Time SMC (FGFTSMC) is derived based on the designed HNCFTSM and an appropriate reaching law. Moreover, to suppress the disturbances polluting the system's dynamics, the control scheme is designed within an ADRC approach. The control design and the stability analysis show that the tracking errors are guaranteed to be fixed-time stable at the equilibrium point without being affected by the deviation of the Initial Conditions (ICs) from the origin. Outdoor flight experiments and comparative analysis are drawn to corroborate the findings of this note. The depicted outcomes approve the effectiveness of the suggested controller in the form of chattering alleviation, disturbance rejection, and uniform fast fixed-time convergence.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Early Stage Diabete Detection by Using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to diabetes prediction, leveraging machine learning algorithms. The study is dedicated to elevating the precision of medical examinations through the application of machine learning to electronic health records (EHRs). In our investigation of the Pima Indian dataset, we employed two distinct strategies-imputation data and, notably, the novel filtered data approach-to address missing values. Subsequently, we rigorously evaluated six supervised machine learning models, encompassing Logistic Regression, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor, Support Vector Machine, XGBoost, and Cat Boost. Metrics including accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and stability were meticulously assessed. Encouragingly, we achieved a commendable 98% accuracy with the Random Forest classifier using the imputation data strategy. However, our groundbreaking contribution lies in the filtered data approach, where we achieved an equally promising 84% accuracy using the XGBoost classifier. This pivotal finding unequivocally establishes the superiority of the filtered data methodology, signifying a significant leap towards enhancing patient risk scoring systems and foreseeing the onset of disease.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models for Classifying Chemical Inhibitors: A Case Study of Aromatase Inhibitors and Pubchem's Molecular Fingerprint Descriptors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In place of traditional experimentation, modern drug development increasingly makes use of machine learning approaches, particularly for making predictions based on the chemical structure of components. As a case study, Aramotase is a catalyst that has been linked to hormonal abnormalities, which in turn can have negative effects on sexual and skeletal maturation. Whereas, it is a major obstacle to create molecules with the aromatase enzyme. Using the ChEMBL database, which at the outset had 2818 compounds of aromatase inhibitors, we offer here a large-scale categorization structure-activity connection analysis. For further investigation, the Ic50 have been chosen as the bioactivity unit. The data curation process resulted in a final dataset consisting of 2071 compounds. We used a methodology to test the performance of different classifiers built using Pubchem's molecular fingerprint descriptors to solve the problem at hand, namely, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, Multilayer Perceptron, and Ad-aBoost. Considering the model's quality metrics, the Multilayer perceptron was considered the most effective model with 80 % for both accuracy and sensitivity for 10-fold cross-validation and 75% and 81 %, respectively, on the test set, and also an Fl-measure of 75%.

articleTitle: Robust Intrusion Detection for IoT Networks: an Integrated CNN-LSTM-GRU Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Ensuring IoT security is of utmost importance in today's interconnected world. IoT devices are prone to various security threats and vulnerabilities, making it essential to implement robust security measures. Intrusion detection plays an instrumental role in safeguarding network information security. However, traditional machine learning techniques face challenges when dealing with large volumes of data and diverse intrusion classes. Consequently, their detection accuracy becomes inadequate, especially when encountering unknown or novel intrusions. In this paper, we introduce a novel Intrusion Detection System (IDS) using Deep Learning (DL) models. The proposed system integrates three powerful DL models, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). Different combination sequences are presented to enhance the system's performance in detecting intrusions by leveraging the strengths of each model. We utilized two datasets: Edge-IIoTset that accurately depicts a network traffic environment consisting of IoT and IIoT applications, and NSL KDD that contains simulated non-real traffic data. We employed several metrics, including accuracy, precision, false positive rate, and detection cost, to assess the system's performance. The experimental results show that our model achieves a perfect accuracy of 100% using Edge-IIoTset in binary classification and an accuracy of 99.95% using the NSL-KDD dataset in multi-class classification. Furthermore, it has an improved detection cost compared to single LSTM and GRU models.

articleTitle: Predicting Student Exam Scores: Exploring the Most Effective Regression Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The incorporation of intelligent technologies, partic-ularly machine learning, has emerged as a pivotal element in the realm of education, warranting diligent attention to the education system. The use of predictive analytics in education presents a challenging yet crucial field, offering valuable insights to educational decision-makers regarding the influential factors that impact student performance. This knowledge enables informed policy decisions based on diverse criteria, thereby facilitating enhanced educational outcomes. This study aims to contribute to this discourse by scrutinising pertinent factors associated with student outcomes. Specifically, public high school students in the United States were interviewed, encompassing a comprehensive range of student-specific, social, and economic factors. To gain deeper insights into the efficacy of student achievement, a diverse set of machine learning algorithms, including Linear Regression (LR), Polynomial Regression (PR), Simple Regression Tree (SRT), Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT), Random Forest (RF), and Tree Ensemble (TE), were used to predict students' writing scores based on the dataset. Among these algorithms, the Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT) model demonstrated exceptional performance, surpassing the others with an impressive R-squared of 0,944.

articleTitle: TwiTrace: A New Approach of Contact Tracing Based on Multilingual Tweets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: By the end of 2019, the world has known a resurgence of epidemics by the sudden outbreak of the COVID-19 virus, that claimed millions of lives, and overwhelmed public health systems. Compared to other known viruses, this one is thought to be more contagious. An individual may be infectious without showing symptoms, so until he tests positive, he might infect many people who meet him. Therefore, to keep the numbers under control, governments apply various strategies such social distancing, remote work and investigative methods like contact tracing to identify potential infected people. Many researchers proposed effective digital contact tracing solutions; nevertheless, they rely on user's cooperation to install applications or to carry sensor devices. However, social networks present a suitable alternative to gather contact-tracing data since they are public and available. In this paper, we propose TwiTrace a new contact tracing approach based on multilingual tweets and graph modelling. TwiTrace creates a dataset for Covid-19 positive cases using Twitter API, and then identifies close contacts and risk places. Next, a graph is generated and queried using Neo4j database. Our approach indicates high accuracy and shows good results in terms of size compared to suspected cases and high-risk places extracted manually.

articleTitle: A Taxonomy of QKA Protocols Based on the BB84
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In Quantum Key Agreement (QKA) protocol, two or more participants agree to share a quantum key. Participants must meet the following conditions: (1) Can be toggled per participant. Important decisions are not made by individual participants. (2) Only participants can access the key, which is not viewable by non-participants while unauthorized acquisition of keys is impossible. Key agreement protocols are used to generate cryptographic keys in many modern applications such as IoT applications, healthcare systems, vehicle communications, intelligent networks, satellite communications, and cloud applications. To resist quantum attacks, several security protocols based on quantum physics principles have been proposed to address various security issues. The main goal of this research is to provide fundamental background information along with a detailed analysis of the theoretical aspects of QKA. The emphasis is particularly on various kinds of multiparty quantum key agreement protocols considering their design and effectiveness, with a specific spotlight on the utilization of the BB84 protocol.

articleTitle: YOLOv7-Face: A Real-Time Face Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Face detection plays a crucial role and serves as a fundamental requirement in several research areas, such as face recognition, face identification, and facial expression analysis, among others. Over the past few years, there has been a rapid growth in deep learning-based algorithms for object detection. These algorithms can be broadly classified into two categories: two-stage detectors, such as Faster R-CNN, and one-stage detectors, such as YOLO. Existing object detection methods aim to strike a balance between speed and accuracy. However, the YOLOv7 algorithm, known for its popularity in object detection, offers clear advantages in terms of both speed and accuracy. In this study, we introduced YOLOv7 as a novel proposed solution for face detection. The proposed method was trained and evaluated on the LFW dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the face detection method based on YOLOv7 exhibits exceptional performance in terms of both speed and accuracy, achieving comparable results to existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques for Alzheimer's Disease Prediction Using CSF and Plasma Biomarkers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease with vast worldwide consequences. Timely and accurate diagnosis is crucial but present methods are costly and resource-intensive. This research work investigates the use of CSF and plasma biomarkers, specifically amyloid beta (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}\beta$</tex>) and tau, in conjunction with machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms to enhance AD prediction. The proposed method seeks to close the gap in accurate early detection and classification. The findings show that improved computational techniques hold the potential to enhance AD diagnosis by leveraging CSF and plasma biomarkers.

articleTitle: Explainable Deep Learning Based-System for Multilabel Classification of 12-Lead ECG
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Deep Learning has made significant strides in classifying Cardiovascular diseases using 12-lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. However, their lack of interpretability poses a significant challenge, thereby limiting their acceptance within the scientific community. This can be attributed to the large number of parameters and the susceptibility of deep neural networks to capturing irrelevant features. To address the challenge, it is crucial to provide explanations for the model's output. This is accomplished through eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), which aims to unravel the “black-box” nature of deep learning models. In this paper, we propose X-ECGNet, an eXplainable multi-branch Convolutional Neural Network designed for multi-label classification of 12-lead ECG signals. Our approach enables the extraction of features from individual leads in the 12-lead ECG independently, which are then combined to maximize the acquisition of information. We leverage this architectural design to generate explanations for each ECG lead using the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) technique. Finally, we evaluate the performance of our model using the PTB-XL dataset, achieving an AUC score of 0.936, thus enhancing both the model's performance and interpretability.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning and Markov Chains Approaches Based Zero Trust Security for Smart Power Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: With the increasing interconnectivity and digitalization of critical infrastructures, such as smart grids, ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is of paramount importance. Industrial Control Systems (ICS) security plays a crucial role in safeguarding the reliable operation of smart grids. In recent years, Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting and mitigating various cybersecurity threats. The application of combined techniques of deep learning and markov chains (MC) within a zero trust model framework for ICS security in smart grids offers significant advantages over traditional rule-based approaches. By leveraging the power of deep learning algorithms, it enables the identification of complex and evolving attack patterns, enhancing the overall security posture of smart grid systems. This paper lays the foundation for further research and development in this field, highlighting the potential of deep learning and Markov chains for addressing the evolving challenges of ICS security in smart grids within a zero trust model framework.

articleTitle: Area Coverage Aware Approach for Data Communication in UAVs Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: The high stability of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and their agility in harsh areas have enabled their effectiveness in several applications in today's research and industrial communities. The proper coordination and collaboration of multiple UAVs wirelessly linked with a central entity as a Flying Ad hoc NETwork (FANET) is vital to organizing data and improving a wide range of tasks. Meanwhile, maintaining connectivity and coverage requirements remain the most critical issues that should be addressed for data communication and mobility patterns in the area of interest. However, there is a conflict between network connectivity and area coverage during network design and maintenance. The aim of this work is to investigate data communication over UAVs networks while optimizing area coverage and exploration. To this end, we propose a new Cluster-based Random Pheromone Zone (C-RDPZ) for data communication and mobility control in UAVs networks. The simulation of the proposed protocol carried out using Network Simulator 3 (NS3) has yielded convincing results in terms of energy consumption, area coverage, and data communication.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Power of Process Mining for Discovering and Analyzing Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Ad hoc networks (MANETs) are dynamic and decentralized systems with diverse applications in wireless communications, social networks, and emergency response systems. Understanding and discovering the underlying structure and behavior of these networks can be challenging due to their spontaneous formation and lack of centralized control. In recent years, process mining techniques have emerged as powerful tools for analyzing and visualizing complex systems, providing valuable insight into their underlying processes. This paper explores the application of process mining techniques to uncover communication patterns, analyze performance metrics, detect anomalies and enable predictive analytics, thereby facilitating better management, optimization, and utilization of these dynamic systems. Using event logs and process discovery algorithms, we delve into the network's structure, communication patterns and emergent behavior. Real-world simulations serve as examples to demonstrate the effectiveness of process mining in uncovering ad hoc networks, shedding light on their functioning, and supporting informed decision-making. The study aims to unleash the power of process mining, enhancing the understanding and analysis of ad hoc networks and leading to improved performance, reliability and security in these decentralized environments.

articleTitle: Real-Time Human Action Representation Based on 2D Skeleton Joints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: We present a new approach to capture human actions by using 2D skeletal joints as the foundation for the real-time representation. Our approach combines three distinct types of information, namely: (1) motion detection to identify salient regions within the action. This allows us to compute joint contribution ratios and save processing time by excluding still joints and focusing on the main joints involved in the action; (2) utilization of a predefined map for joints trajectory shapes, which encodes the temporal information and avoids noisy data using the map; and (3) incorporation of a direction map that captures the movement of the joints, in the spatial space. By integrating these elements, we have devised a comprehensive representation capable of discerning even highly similar actions. To evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed representation, we conducted experiments on the UTD-MHAD dataset [25], which encompasses a diverse range of 27 actions performed by 8 subjects (4 females and 4 males), each with 4 repetitions. The evaluation results exhibit a notable dissimilarity within the same action category (intra-class) and a significant similarity across different action categories (inter-class). Specifically, our approach achieved a commendable score of 94.81 on the UTD-MHAD dataset, thus demonstrating its efficacy and robustness.

articleTitle: Network Applications Observability on Hosts: A New SDN Privacy Issue
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: Software Defined Networking is a relatively new network paradigm that enables unified programmable network control. SDN is still subject to several challenges, such as scalability, availability, security, and reliability. Furthermore, the deployment and expansion of SDN to many specific networks, such as IoT networks, have revealed further challenges, namely privacy issues. Few works in literature have been devoted to certain SDN's privacy problems. In this paper, we highlight a new privacy concern introduced by SDN architecture that has not been considered in the literature. In order to demonstrate the problem and because of the lack of SDN traffic and flow rule datasets, we first implemented Legacy2SDN, a solution for reproducing a legacy network traffic into an SDN environment using PCAP files. We have also implemented a third-party network application that passively collects flow rules and their statistics. Legacy2SDN along with the developed network application are used on a real privacy sensitive network dataset, to conduct experimental case studies to illustrate the privacy issue. Our experimental results prove the observability of network applications on hosts, which can threaten their owners privacy. Finally, we leave the door open for future research in this area by initiating discussion about possible solutions.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Blockchain in Internet of Robotic Things: Advancements, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Networking and Advanced Systems (ICNAS)
abstract: In recent years, the concept of Internet of Robotic Things (IoRT) has gained significant attention, driven by the convergence of robotics, cloud computing, and diverse IoT devices and services. IoRT systems enable the autonomous exchange of data and decision-making within virtual infrastructures. However, managing and controlling diverse robotics applications that interact with IoT devices poses a major challenge in IoRT systems. The conventional centralized approach falls short in providing adequate security and privacy for the IoRT network, particularly due to the mobility of robots and the limited computational and energy resources of IoT devices. To address these limitations, this paper explores the integration of blockchain technology into IoRT networks. Blockchain, known for its distributed ledger based on peer-to-peer communication and trustworthy operations, offers a promising solution. This study provides a comprehensive overview of this integration, starting with an examination of the fundamental characteristics and challenges faced by IoRT networks. It then presents a survey of blockchain technology, highlighting its diverse applications in IoRT systems. Based on our findings, we will propose a new architecture for IoRT that utilizes Blockchain technology to address security and privacy concerns and enhance the overall performance of the network.
